• n inputs → 2ⁿ outputs.

  • The output that turns on is the one whose number matches the input.

Where decoders are used

blocks.html:
• Memory addresses: the processor sends a row number; a decoder switches on that one row of memory.
  • Instructions: the processor reads an instruction’s opcode (the part that says which operation); a decoder turns on the one circuit that does that operation.

Answer: 3
blocks.text:
Asked in: 2026 T2 Quiz 1 · Q2 · 5 marks Question: A 3:8 decoder (A, B, C) has D₂, D₃, D₅, D₆
wired into an OR → Y. Using only 2:1 MUXes, minimum number needed? Answer: 3

blocks.html: How to solve:
blocks.text: How to solve:

blocks.html:
1. Y = Σm(2, 3, 5, 6) = 010, 011, 101, 110
  2. Split on A:
    • A = 0 (rows 0–3): Y = 0, 0, 1, 1 → Y = B
    • A = 1 (rows 4–7): Y = 0, 1, 1, 0 → Y = B ⊕ C
  3. So Y = Ā·B + A·(B ⊕ C) = B ⊕ AC
  4. Build with MUXes (NOT costs a MUX):
    • M1 = MUX(S = A, I₀ = 0, I₁ = C) = AC
    • M2 = MUX(S = M1, I₀ = 1, I₁ = 0) = NOT(AC)
    • Y = MUX(S = B, I₀ = M1, I₁ = M2) = B ⊕ AC
  5. Total 3 ✔ (a computer search confirmed 2 is impossible)

Numbers to remember

blocks.html:
• 2:1 MUX delay = NOT + AND + OR (all 1 ns → 3; NOT 1, AND/OR 2 → 5).
  • Decoder delay = NOT + AND (a 3-input AND made of 2-input ANDs counts twice).
  • 2:1 MUX counts: AND 1, OR 1, NOT 1, XOR 2, XNOR 2, NAND 2, NOR 2.
  • Select lines for an N:1 MUX = log₂N.

Common mistakes

Mistake Correct way

Treating NOT as free in MUX-count questions NOT = 1 MUX (unless the question gives X̅)
Plain encoder with two inputs on Gives a wrong code; that’s why we need priority encoders
Missing a bent wire in a decoder circuit Trace every wire to see which Dₖ goes into the OR
